# DockSplitterProxyPaintNL waits for a drag proxy the dock stopped creating when #17819 made live resize its default

## Context

`DockSplitterProxyPaintNL` is the sixth of the six red workstation/dock e2e arms and the only one still failing. I quarantined it behind `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI` in `#18408` so the new e2e pipeline could run its tier, named the condition rather than a ticket, and took the owner slot. @neo-gpt-emmy's ledger correction made the remaining debt visible; this ticket discharges it.

The other five turned out to be spec defects (`#18410`, `#18412`, `#18415`). So is this one, and its cause is the cleanest of the four.

## The Problem

The arm asserts that crossing the drag threshold on a dock splitter creates a body-mounted drag proxy:

```
Error: crossing the drag threshold must create a splitter proxy
  waiting for locator('body > .neo-dragproxy.neo-dashboard-dock-splitter')
  element(s) not found
```

**There is no proxy, by design, and has not been since `#17819`.**

```js
// src/component/Splitter.mjs
liveResize_: false,                    // base default: proxy-and-commit
useProxy   : !me.liveResize,           // :149 and :267

// src/dashboard/dock/interaction/DockSplitter.mjs
liveResize: true,                      // dock override: proxy-FREE live resize
```

`#17819` introduced proxy-free live sibling resizing, and the dock opted in as its default — its own docblock says so: *"Dock affordances default to the proxy-free main-thread preview … `false` restores the deferred proxy-and-commit presentation."* The spec pins the mechanism that ticket deliberately replaced, so it can only fail.

## Why the Spec Still Has a Job

`#17616` is the regression it was written for: a proxy is a clone mounted at `document.body`, outside the cascade that painted its source, so the `--dock-splitter-*` tokens resolved empty and the affordance vanished at the one moment it exists to say *"you are moving something"*.

Two facts survive `#17819`:

1. **The proxy path still exists** for any consumer running `liveResize: false`, and the token-scope hazard there is unchanged. Deleting the coverage would retire a real guard.
2. **The value generalises past the mechanism.** What `#17616` protects is that the affordance stays painted *while the gesture is live*. Under live resize there is no clone, but there is still a gesture and still a paint that could regress.

A spec asserting one presentation cannot see the other, which is how a default flip left a guard pinned to a dead branch with nobody noticing until the arm went red for an unrelated-looking reason.

## The Fix

Parameterise over both presentations rather than choosing one:

- **`liveResize: true`** (the dock default) — the splitter itself stays painted, with its handle metric intact, while the drag is held.
- **`liveResize: false`** — the proxy resolves the tokens its source was painted with. The `#17616` guard, preserved verbatim in intent.

Then remove the `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI` quarantine, which returns the arm to the CI tier `#18408` established.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both presentations are exercised, and each names which one it measured on failure.
- [ ] The `liveResize: false` arm still fails if the proxy loses its token scope — verified by breaking the projection, not by inspection.
- [ ] The `liveResize: true` arm asserts on a held gesture, not at rest: a resting assertion re-certifies the surface that was never broken, which is how `#17616` passed review in the first place.
- [ ] The quarantine guard is deleted, not weakened, and `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs` no longer lists the arm.
- [ ] The tier's selection floor still passes with the quarantine entry removed.

## Out of Scope

- The live-resize commit path itself (`#17819`'s own witnesses cover it).
- The remaining `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI` uses elsewhere in the suite.

## Related

- `#17616` — the proxy paint regression this arm was written for.
- `#17819` — introduced proxy-free live resize and flipped the dock's default.
- `#18408` — quarantined the arm so the e2e tier could ship; this releases it.
